page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU core. This hardware profile focuses processing resources toward compute density rather than large in-memory capacities.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for all persistent data and operating system needs. It includes no hardware accelerator GPUs. On the networking side, ecs.c8i.8xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps without any complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration delivers high processing capacity without incurring the expense of excess memory capacity. However, environments with intense I/O requirements must account for the dependence on remote storage over network attachments, as local NVMe or SSD options are absent.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.8xlarge is structured for compute-heavy workloads that match its 32-core allocation and 20 Gbps network pipe. Typical application targets include distributed batch processing, high-traffic web servers, application backend tiers, continuous integration and deployment compilation nodes, and stateless computational services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8475B x86_64 processor offering 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for system disks and operational data, and it includes no discrete GPU hardware. By balancing high vCPU counts with moderate memory sizing, the instance maintains cost efficiency for computational duties that do not demand extensive memory allocations. Best-fit use cases include distributed compilation, high-volume web serving, stateless microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and batch computational jobs.
